questions.question: In the study of Radical Reactions, what is the authoritative chemical definition of 'Free Radical'?

options.label: B
options.text: A substance (e.g., BHT, hydroquinone, Vitamin E) that rapidly traps and scavenges active chain-propagating radicals to terminate radical cascades.

options.label: D
options.text: A chemical compound containing a weak bond (e.g., peroxides RO-OR or AIBN) that homolytically cleaves with heat or light (hν) to generate initiating free radicals.

options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Anti-Markovnikov Hydrobromination is properly defined as: A bond fission process where a covalent bond breaks symmetrically so that each separating atom receives one of the two shared electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Anti-Markovnikov Hydrobromination is properly defined as: A chemical compound containing a weak bond (e.g., peroxides RO-OR or AIBN) that homolytically cleaves with heat or light (hν) to generate initiating free radicals.

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Anti-Markovnikov Hydrobromination is properly defined as: A neutral, highly reactive chemical species containing an unpaired electron in an unhybridized atomic or molecular orbital.
